summary: Redwood walked CardioHealth through capabilities for EU data residency, region pinning, and cross-border processing controls. Customer required EU-only processing for PHI-adjacent telemetry and strict sub-processor visibility. Discussed private deployment options, VPC/private control plane, KMS integration, audit log retention and RBAC/SSO. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, schedule EU pilot, and exchange DPA comments.
topics: Cross-border processing and lawful transfer mechanisms
Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM integration
Audit logs, retention, and access controls
Private/VPC deployment vs hosted with EU region
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood inference, i'll kick us off. 00:05 Marta Alvarez: hi jordan, thanks. we have about 45 minutes. we really want to focus on data residency and region pinning — our legal and compliance teams flagged EU-only processing for a subset of workloads. 00:15 Jordan Lee: got it, that's exactly what priya (our se) and samir can cover. quick intro from our side? priya? 00:22 Priya Nair: hey all, priya nair, se focusing on deployments and security. i'll walk through region pinning, routing, and the KMS integration. 00:30 Ethan Park: quick background — cardiohealth runs patient-facing triage and backend analytics, some workloads are regulated under european privacy regs and we need zero cross-border processing for that subset. 00:40 Priya Nair: right, so we have two main approaches: hosted EU-only endpoints where compute and storage are pinned to eu-west regions, or private deployment (vpc/on-prem) where the control plane is customer-managed. both support per-route region pinning and per-tenant model version locks. 00:56 Marta Alvarez: can you explain what you mean by "pinned"? we want absolute assurance that data and model cache never leave eu. 01:05 Priya Nair: yes — pinned means the request routing and runtime lifecycle are constrained to selected regions. for hosted, requests to an EU-pinned route route to eu-hosted clusters only, kv cache and ephemeral token caches are created in-region, and persistent logs/metrics for that tenant are stored in our eu data stores. 01:20 Noah Chen: what about failover? if eu capacity is exhausted, does traffic go to us by default? that's a dealbreaker. 01:29 Samir Patel: good question — we have configurable fallback policies. default for EU-pinned routes is "no cross-border fallback" which will return capacity errors; alternative is "regional fallback" but that must be explicitly enabled. 01:41 Ethan Park: how does this interact with the model catalog? do models need to be provisioned per-region? 01:48 Priya Nair: model artifacts are replicated per-region when you request pinned deployments. we maintain model version manifests and ensure inference kernels and weights are resident in the chosen region. replication is done under our sub-processor agreements, and you can opt to bring-your-own model to avoid cross-subproc replication. 02:02 Lina Gomez: bring-your-own sounds promising but can we still get security attestations if we host models ourselves? 02:07 Jordan Lee: yes — for private deployments we provide the enterprise package including installation guides and checklist; we also share network diagrams, and we can support audited KMS integrations so keys never leave your environment. 02:16 Marta Alvarez: about KMS — we need to use our cloud kms (we use google cloud kms in eu), can you integrate? 02:21 Priya Nair: we support both customer-managed keys in cloud kms and external HSMs for private installs. for hosted with customer-managed keys, the encryption-at-rest keys are stored in your cloud KMS and we perform envelope encryption; Redwood only sees ciphertext. 02:34 Noah Chen: any latencies or operational caveats when using CMKs? 02:38 Samir Patel: minimal impact — key unwrap occurs at instance startup and for occasional metadata operations. per-token inference path uses symmetric keys cached in-memory; we don't call KMS per token. 02:50 Marta Alvarez: logs — we need audit logs for every API call, who accessed what, and retention for seven years for compliance. is that supported? 02:58 Priya Nair: yes, we have audit logging at the tenant and token level. retention is configurable; hosted offers up to 7 years as an add-on, and logs can be exported to your SIEM or to EU-only cloud storage via our retention connectors. 03:14 Ethan Park: export to our splunk in eu — is that agentless pull or push? 03:18 Priya Nair: we push via secure transfer—s3-compatible encrypted endpoints or push to your splunk ingest over TLS. connectors run inside our eu region for pinned tenants. 03:29 Marta Alvarez: what's the position on sub-processors? our procurement needs a list. 03:34 Jordan Lee: standard sub-processor list includes cloud providers (aws/gcp/azure depending on region), logging vendors, and a monitoring SaaS. we provide an up-to-date sub-processor list and contract language in the dpa. you can request EU-only sub-processor footprint and we can restrict services to providers with eu data centers. 03:50 Lina Gomez: do you support SCCs or other lawful transfer mechanisms? 03:54 Jordan Lee: yes, our DPA includes standard SCCs where applicable; for customers requiring it we can negotiate EU data transfer addenda or push for in-region-only hosting to avoid transfers. 04:05 Marta Alvarez: ok, about SOC2/ISO — we asked for reports earlier, can you deliver? 04:10 Jordan Lee: we'll send SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate in the security packet after this call. 04:14 Lina Gomez: please mark any redactions and list the scope (which systems are in-scope). 04:19 Jordan Lee: will do. 04:21 Ethan Park: want to talk about PII / PHI handling — some of our messages are PHI-adjacent. does redwood do any content scanning or retention by default? 04:30 Priya Nair: by default we retain short-term logs for observability; retention is configurable per-tenant. for regulated data we recommend pinned routes + minimal retention and explicit "no-logging" flags on routes. we also support automatic PII masking and opa-based policies to block certain classes of data from being persisted. 04:47 Noah Chen: does masking happen before it leaves our network? 04:51 Samir Patel: if you run private deployment it's inside your VPC, so masking occurs in-region. for hosted, masking and redaction components run in-region for pinned workloads. 04:59 Marta Alvarez: curious about RBAC and SSO — our admins must be in our SAML IdP and must not be able to escalate. 05:06 Priya Nair: Redwood supports SAML2.0 and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC roles. you can map IdP groups to roles and restrict actions like model-promotion, key-rotation, and audit-log access. we also provide an admin activity trail. 05:22 Ethan Park: how granular is RBAC? can we scope to per-route or per-environment? 05:26 Priya Nair: yes — roles can be scoped to projects, routes, and models. you can create a role that only allows inference but not model uploads or billing. 05:36 Lina Gomez: we need to see example policy templates for SOC2 audits. 05:39 Jordan Lee: we'll include policy templates and proof points in the packet. 05:42 Marta Alvarez: subprocessors again — if you use a monitoring vendor with servers outside eu, does that count as cross-border processing? 05:50 Jordan Lee: yes, technically. that's why we provide the option to restrict which sub-processors are used for a tenant; for EU-pinned tenants we prefer vendors with eu footprint or alternative connectors that send telemetry to your EU-only collector. 06:04 Noah Chen: network controls — we need to be able to VPC-peering or private link to avoid public internet. 06:10 Samir Patel: supported — we offer private link, VPC peering, and in private deployments you can keep traffic fully internal. for hosted, data-in-flight is TLS with mTLS options for private links. 06:22 Ethan Park: are there any exceptions where metadata is stored outside eu, like usage billing or aggregated metrics? 06:29 Priya Nair: we try to keep tenant metadata in-region; aggregated anonymized metrics might be stored in central telemetry for product improvement, but for enterprise packages we can opt out and keep even aggregated metrics in-region. we'll document scope in the DPA. 06:45 Marta Alvarez: contractual — will you accept clause that requires all processing to remain in eu for specified routes and an audit right? 06:52 Jordan Lee: yes, enterprise DPAs include processing location commitments and an audit clause; we do annual third-party audits and can provide logs for agreed audits. 07:02 Lina Gomez: about retention — do you support legal hold for records? 07:06 Priya Nair: yes, retention and legal hold are supported; we can freeze deletes and export logs for e-discovery. 07:12 Marta Alvarez: excellent. last technical question: model cache — does kv cache get persisted to disk? 07:16 Samir Patel: kv caches are in-memory by default; if we do checkpointing for large models in private deployments it's encrypted at rest and keys are customer-managed in EU for pinned setups. 07:28 Ethan Park: ok let's recap next steps. 07:31 Jordan Lee: recap — jordan will send soc2, priya will send region-pinning doc and config, samir will coordinate private link/VPC details, customer will supply perf dataset and legal will send dpa redlines. 07:44 Marta Alvarez: great, thanks everyone. 07:46 Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up by email with the security packet and proposed dates for the pilot. 07:50 [meeting ends]
